name: Levator scapulae stretch
summary: Turn the head toward one armpit and gently draw it down with the hand until the side of the neck stretches.
setup: Sit facing the phone, one hand holding the chair edge to keep that shoulder down. Turn the head toward the opposite armpit and rest the other hand on the back of the head. Let it draw the head gently down. Hold.
brief: Sit tall, one hand holding the chair edge to keep that shoulder down. Turn the head toward the opposite armpit, rest the other hand on the back of the head, and hold.
why: Facing the phone, the gap between ear and shoulder on the stretched side opens as the head goes down, so the timer only runs while you are actually in the stretch.
tempo: Ease in 5 s, hold, ease out.
progression: Hold the chair to anchor the shoulder more firmly.
regression: No hand on the head; turn and look down only.
contraindications: Dizziness, or pain or tingling into the arm.

faults.label: Stretched-side shoulder rising
faults.tip: Hold the seat of the chair so the shoulder stays anchored; the stretch comes from the head, not the shoulder.

faults.label: Pulling hard with the hand
faults.cue: Let the hand rest, do not pull
faults.tip: The hand is a weight resting on the head. Pulling makes the muscle guard.

faults.label: Not turning the head far enough
faults.tip: The levator stretch needs the head turned about 45° before it tips — straight down is the trapezius.

faults.label: Stretched shoulder lifting
faults.tip: Anchor the shoulder by sitting on the hand, or the stretch goes nowhere.

guide.surface: A chair with an edge to hold.
guide.cannotSee: How hard the hand is pulling.

points.t: Turned toward the armpit and drawn gently down.
Anchored down on the stretched side.
